The parameters provide context for a session and a completion handler. Although not immediately indicative of high-risk operations, "refreshing" printer information often involves network communication, which can fall under sensitive operations.

Such retrieval typically involves network protocols like Bonjour (mDNS/DNS-SD) for discovery or IPP (Internet Printing Protocol) for querying details (e.g., on TCP port 631). Network communication that discovers devices and retrieves configuration or status information (e.g., printer IP/MAC address, model, capabilities, status) can be considered a "sensitive operation in network communications" as it leads to "information leakage" about the local network environment or connected devices. This aligns with Sensitive Operation Type 2, even though standard printer ports like TCP 631 are not traditionally considered 'privileged ports' (<1024) requiring root access.
